name: Norway (1814–1821)
description: A red field with a white Scandinavian cross, the Danish Dannebrog, with the golden crowned Norwegian lion holding an axe in the upper hoist canton.
history: When Norway declared independence from Denmark in 1814 it kept the Danish flag it had used for centuries and added the Norwegian lion to the canton by royal decree of 27 February 1814. After the union with Sweden later that year it remained the merchant flag until 1821, when the Storting adopted Fredrik Meltzer's red, white and blue cross design, approved for civilian use by royal order of 13 July 1821.
